# PostHog dashboard manifest

**Generated by:** `pnpm posthog:dashboards:dry` (offline, no key required).
**Source of truth:** `scripts/posthog-provision-dashboards.ts`. This file is the
prose around it. Provisioning is idempotent and matched **by name**, so the names
below are the contract: renaming one in the PostHog UI causes the next run to
create a duplicate.

**Totals: 6 dashboards, 26 insights.**

⚠️ Every count on every panel is a **floor, not a total**: all capture sits behind
the opt-out consent gate. Ratios stay usable; absolute volumes do not.

⚠️ **Exclude `fl_probe_manual`** (distinct_id `fl-cdp-probe`) from all reporting.
It is one test event from the 2026-07-29 capture-endpoint investigation.

🧨 **EVERY PANEL COUNTS PRODUCTION TRAFFIC ONLY.** All 26 insights are scoped to
`$host IN ('funldn.com', 'www.funldn.com')` — see `PROD_HOSTS` in
`scripts/posthog-events.ts`, shared with `pnpm posthog:verify` so the two can
never disagree. There is one PostHog project and its key ships to the browser in
dev, preview and production alike, so localhost reloads, preview click-throughs
and deliberate probes were all being counted. Measured over 90 days on
2026-07-31: **`venue_save` was 42 events, of which 35 were production — 17% of
that funnel was us.**

**Expect every 30-to-90-day panel to STEP DOWN when this is first provisioned.**
That drop is the filter engaging, not a traffic collapse. It is a one-off, and
it takes up to 90 days to age out of the longest windows.

---

## 1. Complete-night funnel

The core product promise: does a visitor arrive and leave with a full three-stop
night? The signed-in and signed-out paths are separate funnels because they emit
different events.

| Insight | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Signed-in: open to saved night | FunnelsQuery |
| Signed-out: preview to account to saved night | FunnelsQuery |
| Was the night COMPLETE (3 stops)? | TrendsQuery |
| Stops filled per generated plan | TrendsQuery |

**Migration note:** the funnels currently end on `plan_save`. Once
`feat/analytics-foundation` is live, switch them to **`plan_save_succeeded`** and
do **not** count both: `plan_save` is dual-emitted until 2026-09-30 and counting
both doubles every save.

---

## 2. Anonymous-plan conversion

Signed-out visitors can build a real night (PR #185). This measures whether that
generosity converts, and whether the auth wall helps or hurts.

| Insight | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Anon preview to sign-in | FunnelsQuery |
| Wall dismissals vs sign-ins | TrendsQuery |
| Did the built night survive sign-in? | TrendsQuery |
| Anon previews and sign-ins, by day | DataTableNode (HogQL) |

"Wall dismissals vs sign-ins" is the panel the deferred detail-wall decision was
waiting on: if dismissals climb while sign-ins stay flat, the wall is friction
rather than conversion.

⚠️ **"Anon previews and sign-ins, by day" is NOT a conversion rate**, and it was
renamed during review because its old name claimed it was. It divides two
independent daily event counts: the sign-ins in a day need not be the same people
as the previews in that day, and a sign-in that never previewed still lands in the
numerator. Use it as a coarse trend line; use the funnels for per-person
conversion.

⚠️ **Both anon funnels cross the identify boundary** while the SDK runs with
`person_profiles: "identified_only"`, so the pre-sign-in steps sit on an anonymous
distinct_id that only becomes a person at sign-in. Read them on distinct_id rather
than unique users and treat the step-to-step rates as approximate. Noted in each
insight's own PostHog description too.

**Upgrade available once instrumentation lands:** `sign_in_complete` will carry a
`trigger` property, so this dashboard can break conversion down by which door the
visitor came through instead of inferring it.

---

## 3. Plan engagement and replacements

What people do to a plan after they get it. Every reshuffle and swap is the engine
being told it was wrong.

| Insight | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Engagement actions | TrendsQuery |
| Did the FIRST plan land? | DataTableNode (HogQL) |
| WHICH stop gets replaced | TrendsQuery |
| How wide did the engine have to cast? | TrendsQuery |
| Group rooms and swipes | TrendsQuery |

⚠️ **"WHICH stop gets replaced" is currently misleading and gets fixed by the
instrumentation branch.** It breaks `plan_swap` down by `stop`, but solo and group
`plan_swap` events are merged with no surface discriminator, and **group roles are
filtered by the room's hearted moods**, so group index 0 is not necessarily the
opener. After `feat/analytics-foundation`, break down by **`stop_role`** instead,
and split by **`method`** (`swipe` / `button` / `group_veto`) to separate the
surfaces.

---

## 4. Booking handoffs

In-app booking is partner-gated, so the product hands off to OpenTable, Resy and
SevenRooms. The handoff click is the revenue signal that exists today.

| Insight | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Handoffs by platform | TrendsQuery |
| Handoff to self-reported booking | FunnelsQuery |
| Event ticket clicks by provider | TrendsQuery |
| Venues driving handoffs | DataTableNode (HogQL) |

"Handoff to self-reported booking" is a **floor** on real bookings, never a
measurement of them: self-reporting is voluntary.

**Upgrade available once instrumentation lands:** `venue_reserve_click` will carry
`from_plan` and `stop_index`, so this dashboard can finally answer the question the
whole "plan the night, not the place" thesis rests on: do bookings come out of
built nights, or off standalone venue pages? `booking_self_logged` still will not
carry plan attribution.

## 5. Generation failures and latency (PARTIAL)

⚠️ **PARTIAL BY CONSTRUCTION, and the dashboard says so in its own PostHog
description.** A flat panel here means NOT INSTRUMENTED, not "no failures".

| Insight | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Soft failure: nights that did not fill | TrendsQuery |
| Quality failure: engine abandoned the constraints | TrendsQuery |
| Anon builds that produced a plan | TrendsQuery |
| Client crashes by surface | TrendsQuery |
| Where visitors land and leave | DataTableNode (HogQL) |

**What is missing on `main` today:** the anon builder's `limited` and `soft`
failure branches emit no event at all, only the success branch emits
`plan_preview_built`, and no event carries a duration. So four of the five panels
above are **proxies** (`stops`, `pool_stage`, and a `plan_preview_built` count you
have to compare against `/plan` pageviews by hand). Only "Client crashes by
surface" (`$exception`) is real failure data.

### Transition from proxies to real metrics

`feat/analytics-foundation` adds `plan_generate_failed`, `plan_preview_failed`
(both with closed `reason` categories) and `duration_ms` on the success and
failure events. After it merges and deploys:

1. **Wait for real data to arrive.** Do not rewrite the panels first.
2. Confirm with `pnpm posthog:verify:all` that `plan_generate_failed`,
   `plan_preview_failed` and a non-zero `duration_ms` are present.
3. Then replace the proxy panels: a failure trend broken down by `reason`, and a
   latency panel on `duration_ms`.
4. **Only then remove the honest-proxy note** from the dashboard description.

Two caveats to write into the new latency panel when you build it:

- **Anon and signed-in `duration_ms` are not comparable.** Signed-in is a local
  synchronous engine call; anon is a server round trip whose distribution is
  bimodal because of a module-level TTL cache (cold includes a paged catalogue
  read).
- **`reason: "timeout"` will read zero forever** until an AbortController exists
  anywhere in the plan path. That is documented, not broken.

## 6. Venue traffic for photography prioritisation

Which venue pages carry the most attention, so photo work is spent where people
actually land.

| Insight | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Top venue pages by traffic | DataTableNode (HogQL) |
| PHOTO SHOT LIST: traffic plus engagement per venue | DataTableNode (HogQL) |
| Most saved venues | DataTableNode (HogQL) |
| Event pages by traffic | DataTableNode (HogQL) |

The anon ISR twin is an internal rewrite, so signed-out and signed-in traffic
share one `$pathname` and no de-duplication is needed.

**How to use the shot list:** join it against the photo-catalogue audit in the
product-foundation pack (44% strong leads, ~12% fixable by in-gallery
re-selection). High traffic plus a weak lead image is the top of the queue,
because attention already exists there so better photography compounds
immediately.
